summary.title: Cybersecurity News Briefing: Active Exploitation, Ransomware, and Major Breaches

overview.executive_summary: The most consequential developments include multiple vulnerabilities under active exploitation, ransomware disruptions affecting healthcare and business services, large-scale data breaches, and significant security responses. Several candidate reports describe the same events, which have been consolidated here.

sections.heading: CISA adds two actively exploited vulnerabilities to KEV
sections.what_happened: CISA added Adobe Commerce and Magento CVE-2026-48356 and Google Brotli CVE-2026-111497 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation.
sections.why_it_matters: The catalog additions identify vulnerabilities being used in attacks and highlight risks to affected systems.
sections.recommended_attention: Prioritize remediation and assess publicly exposed assets for compromise.

sections.heading: PHP2Shell vulnerabilities exploited in attacks
sections.what_happened: CISA confirmed active exploitation of two PHP2Shell vulnerabilities and added them to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog.
sections.why_it_matters: The flaws enable unauthenticated remote code execution on affected deployments.
sections.recommended_attention: Patch affected PHP deployments urgently and investigate for exploitation.

sections.heading: Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day involved three chained flaws
sections.what_happened: Researchers reported that the critical Oracle PeopleSoft issue exploited by ShinyHunters consisted of three chained flaws. Oracle patched them under CVE-2026-35273.
sections.why_it_matters: The chain includes server-side request forgery reaching an internal management interface, demonstrating a serious path to compromise.
sections.recommended_attention: Confirm that the Oracle patch is applied and review relevant access and application logs.

sections.heading: UNM Health ransomware attack disrupts patient care
sections.what_happened: The University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center disclosed a cyberattack that caused system outages and disrupted patient care, surgeries, and academic activities.
sections.why_it_matters: Operational disruption in a healthcare environment can directly affect patients and clinical services.
sections.recommended_attention: Track restoration and continuity measures while assessing the incident’s scope.

sections.heading: GMO offers reward after Desktop Cloud breach
sections.what_happened: Japan’s GMO Internet Group offered up to $1 million for information leading to the arrest or international wanted notice of attackers who breached its Onamae.com Desktop Cloud service.
sections.why_it_matters: The service hosts Windows desktops used for foreign-exchange trading, and the company refused to pay an extortion demand.
sections.recommended_attention: Monitor customer guidance, service impact, and further breach disclosures.

sections.heading: University of Copenhagen breach affects 525,000 people
sections.what_happened: Hackers accessed a University of Copenhagen test environment containing personal data belonging to 525,000 people.
sections.why_it_matters: The reported scale makes this a major personal-data exposure.
sections.recommended_attention: Follow the university’s investigation and assess notification and identity-risk implications.

sections.heading: Cybercrime operation stole 8.2 million records
sections.what_happened: South Korean police identified seven suspects linked to attacks on more than 90 organizations, with the ARTEX AI pentesting framework used in most attacks. The operation stole 8.2 million data records.
sections.why_it_matters: The campaign combined broad victim targeting with an AI-assisted offensive tool.
sections.recommended_attention: Review exposure to the named attack pattern and strengthen monitoring for unauthorized testing activity.

sections.heading: Adobe patches eight critical Campaign Classic flaws
sections.what_happened: Adobe released patches for eight critical Campaign Classic vulnerabilities that could enable arbitrary code execution, security feature bypass, and privilege escalation.
sections.why_it_matters: The vulnerabilities include a code-injection flaw rated 9.9 that could lead to arbitrary code execution.
sections.recommended_attention: Apply Adobe’s fixes and verify that Campaign Classic systems are not exposed.

sections.heading: Tailscale fixes SSH flaws enabling root access
sections.what_happened: Tailscale released version 1.104.4 to fix flaws in its built-in SSH server that could let attackers reach services and files on other servers accessible only to root.
sections.why_it_matters: The issues could allow compromised devices to extend access into other systems.
sections.recommended_attention: Update Tailscale and review SSH activity on systems using the affected functionality.

sections.heading: Australia disrupts Amadey malware infrastructure
sections.what_happened: Australia’s Signals Directorate said its operators gained access to the Amadey malware backend and cut it off from 180,000 infected computers worldwide, including some in Australia.
sections.why_it_matters: The action stopped the criminal operator from accessing or stealing data from those computers.
sections.recommended_attention: Use the disruption as an opportunity to identify and remediate any remaining Amadey infections.

sections.heading: Dahua cameras hijacked in Ukraine
sections.what_happened: Ukraine’s CERT warned of unauthorized remote access to Dahua video surveillance systems, including access to video streams, configuration changes, and creation of third-party accounts.
sections.why_it_matters: Compromised cameras can expose surveillance feeds and provide attackers with persistent device access.
sections.recommended_attention: Audit Dahua devices, accounts, configurations, and remote-access settings.

sections.heading: Microsoft Authenticator flaw exposed work-account tokens
sections.what_happened: Microsoft fixed an Android Authenticator flaw that allowed a malicious app with no permissions to impersonate a trusted Microsoft app and collect work-account sign-in tokens. The fix is in version 6.2606.4246.
sections.why_it_matters: Stolen tokens could undermine account authentication even without traditional permission requests.
sections.recommended_attention: Update Authenticator for Android and review suspicious work-account activity.

tts.text: Here’s your cybersecurity briefing. CISA added two vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog, including flaws in Adobe Commerce and Google’s Brotli library. CISA also confirmed active exploitation of two PHP2Shell vulnerabilities that enable unauthenticated remote code execution. Oracle PeopleSoft’s exploited zero-day was found to involve three chained flaws. In ransomware news, an attack on the University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center disrupted patient care and surgeries. Japan’s GMO offered up to one million dollars for information about attackers who breached its desktop cloud service. The University of Copenhagen reported a breach affecting data belonging to five hundred twenty-five thousand people, while a South Korean operation allegedly stole 8.2 million records from more than 90 organizations using the ARTEX AI framework. Adobe patched eight critical Campaign Classic flaws, and Tailscale fixed SSH issues that could enable root-level access. Australia disrupted Amadey malware control over 180,000 computers. Finally, Ukraine warned that Dahua cameras were being hijacked, and Microsoft fixed an Authenticator flaw that exposed work-account tokens.
